title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The Providing Green Graduation Opportunities to Households Living in Conditions of Extreme Poverty in Tanganyika Province, DRC programme will work in Manono, Kabalo and Kongolo, Democratic Republic of Congo. It aims to contribute to Concern DRC’s Green Graduation thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to graduate vulnerable households out of conditions of extreme poverty and support communities to be more inclusive and resilient in Tanganyika, with emphasis placed on improved environmental protection and sustainability. The programme will support over 147,960 people living in extreme poor households, including female headed households, households with disabled members, households with pregnant and lactating women. This will be done through households having access to a predictable source of income to cover their basic needs, households receive farmer field schools trainings, households receive life skills and literacy training, gender transformative discussions held for beneficiaries and partners and improved social cohesion in target communities .. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Improving the resilience and the capacity of vulnerable populations in Beni, Grand Nord Kivu to cope with recurring shocks.. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: RM Adaptation 2: With this allocation, the green graduation (GG) programme in DRC will conduct a Climate Vulnerability and Capacity Assessment (CVCA) with the support of Head Office technical advisors. The purpose of the CVCA will be to support LTD GG communities to identify contextual climate shocks, stresses and changes that are impacting their ability to secure their basic needs. Communities will then be supported to develop Community Adaptation Action Plans (CAAPs) to address areas where communities can be empowered to make a positive difference in their resilience at the household or community level. The intention is that elements of these plans will be financed through the Climate Allocation in 2025.DRR 1: Green Graduation programmes are intended to build the resilience of communities and natural systems to a changing climate through awareness raising, capacity building, environmental awareness and promoting climate-smart activities.Aid to Environment 1: Concern’s Green Graduation programme added a 5th pillar to the traditional graduation model - the ‘green’ aspect which aims to improve environmental protection and stability through awareness raising, capacity building, assessing environmental impacts, reducing and managing environmental risks and increasing natural assets.Capacity Building 1: building the capacity of communities on climate-smart activities is necessary for environmental protection and sustainability.Gender Equality 1: a gender lens is applied at every stage and a gender transformative approach is taken to tackle harmful gender norms, attitudes and practices.Nutrition 1: Through improved agricultural practices (increasing yields) and messaging on nutrition, the nutritional status of HHs is improved.
